done.why: Every route past the troll room was blocked by an unfinished-passage note or a refused hole, so I ran out of places to go.

about: A small cut-down version of the Zork opening: the house, the cellar and the troll room. The deeper caverns are not built yet.

moments.note: The troll eats the pepper sack and the bottle, and gives nothing back.
The sword killed the troll very quickly: it was confused after eating, then died on the next blow.
The crawlway to the south: digging that stops politely until you back out.
The east passage and the west hole are dead ends. The east one has a 'Back soon, The Management' note.
'South' from the troll room printed only 'Cellar', with none of the usual room description.

wished: Go further into the caverns past the troll room.
Listen to the digging, or find out who is behind it.
Put water into the sack, or otherwise combine items.

lines.line: From somewhere beyond it comes the sound of digging, which stops, politely, until you have backed out.
lines.why: The funniest and most characterful line in the game.

lines.line: The passage to the east has not been finished. A note is pinned to the rock: "Back soon. -- The Management."
lines.why: A playful way to mark the edge of the built world.

fun.why: Familiar puzzles with a few charming twists, but it ended quickly.

engagement.why: Good pull at first, then it ran dry at the dead ends.

difficulty.why: The troll fell almost immediately and nothing blocked progress until the unfinished edge.

interestingness.why: The changes to the classic (the troll eating gifts, the digging) are intriguing, but there was little to explore.

prose.why: Short, witty lines, especially the digging and the Management note.
